events.title: Seneca Falls Convention Opens
events.description: The first women's rights convention in the United States began in Seneca Falls, New York, organized by Elizabeth Cady Stanton, Lucretia Mott, and others. The gathering continued into July 20 and produced the Declaration of Sentiments, modeled on the Declaration of Independence, which demanded equal rights for women including the right to vote.
events.significance: Marked the formal beginning of the organized women's suffrage movement in the United States, laying the groundwork for the 19th Amendment in 1920.

events.title: Opening of the First Line of the Paris Métro
events.description: The first line of the Paris Métro, Line 1, opened between Porte de Vincennes and Porte Maillot, just in time to serve visitors to the 1900 Exposition Universelle held in the city.
events.significance: Began one of the world's most iconic and densely used urban rapid transit systems, which influenced urban transit design and became a symbol of Parisian life.

events.title: Discovery of the Rosetta Stone
events.description: French soldiers under Napoleon's Egyptian campaign, while strengthening fortifications near the town of Rashid (Rosetta), uncovered a granodiorite stele inscribed with a decree in three scripts: Egyptian hieroglyphic, Demotic, and ancient Greek.
events.significance: The stone provided the key that allowed Jean-François Champollion to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs in the 1820s, opening ancient Egyptian civilization to modern scholarship.

events.title: Sandinista Revolution Triumphs in Nicaragua
events.description: The Sandinista National Liberation Front (FSLN) took power in Managua after the fall of dictator Anastasio Somoza Debayle, who had fled the country days earlier, ending over four decades of rule by the Somoza family.
events.significance: The revolution reshaped Nicaraguan politics and became a major Cold War flashpoint in Central America, leading to the U.S.-backed Contra war and the Iran-Contra affair.

events.title: Moscow Summer Olympics Open
events.description: The Games of the XXII Olympiad opened in Moscow, the first Olympics held in Eastern Europe. They were affected by a boycott led by the United States and joined by dozens of other nations in protest of the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.
events.significance: Highlighted the intrusion of Cold War politics into international sport and led to a retaliatory Soviet-led boycott of the 1984 Los Angeles Games.
